tolerance.notes: longlat is the geographic WGS84 identity: forward x = lon - lon_0, forward y = lat; inverse-of-forward = identity. The maps are exact subtractions/additions of Float64 degrees, so at the integer-valued coords/lon_0 below every value is byte-exact; the 1e-12 absolute band is a conservative cross-binding floor (RFC pure-io-data-loaders §8: 'cross-binding byte-identical where the closed-form is exact'). The reference binding drives reprojection/longlat.esm through the ESS engine via the zero-IC surfacing idiom (d(forward_x)/dt = proj_x from a zero IC, so du = the map value).

cases.name: wgs84_lon0_0
cases.notes: WGS84 default central meridian: the forward map IS the geographic identity (x = lon) and the round-trip equals the input EXACTLY.

cases.name: shifted_lon0_10
cases.notes: Non-zero central meridian: lon_0 is LOAD-BEARING (forward x = lon - 10 != lon), the declarative-or-fail proof the format binds a parameterized transform; the inverse-of-forward round-trip stays the identity.

cases.name: shifted_lon0_neg73p5
cases.notes: Fractional central meridian (still exactly representable): forward x = lon + 73.5.

cases.name: shifted_lon0_180
cases.notes: Antimeridian central meridian: forward x = lon - 180 (no longitude wrapping in the identity projection).
